ERR-001 • Blacksburg, Virginia (Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute / CPI) • 1985–Present (2004–2014 Burnout Hiatus)

The Stardust Engine

80s Synth-Pop, Progressive Arena Rock & The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™

The founding five-member family unit behind Engine Room Records. Forged at Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) in 1985–1986 by siblings Ryan, Cassidy, and Holly O'Connell and identical twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright, The Stardust Engine blends soaring 1980s stadium synth-rock with Cassidy's zero-gravity Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™.

What Kind of Music Is The Stardust Engine? High-energy 1980s stadium AOR, driving analog synthesizers, sibling vocal duets, progressive rock suites (including the 15-minute "Escape Velocity / Ad Astra"), and lush zero-gravity "80s Cosmic Pop."

Canonical In-Universe History

1. Canonical Band Lore & Sanctuary History

The 1986 Band Name Canon ("Stardust" + "Engine")

In 1986, when identical twin cousins Evan and Tyler Wright joined Cassidy and Ryan O'Connell at CPI, the very first song the four of them wrote together was "The Stardust Engine"—celebrating their shared love of the cosmos ("Stardust") and the rockets to get you there ("Engine"). Too scared to shop the song around at first, they used its title to name the band before releasing it in 1987 as Track 13 on Electric Color. When Apex Records signed them, Apex executives cheaply branded Cassidy as their "Stardust" and Ryan as their "Engine"—a 1980s corporate marketing gimmick the band despises because it strips away their genuine love of the cosmos and rocket propulsion.

The 1992 "Friction" Emancipation & Birth of the Fortress

After Ryan's December 1990 spinal cord injury, Apex executive Julian Vance attempted to coerce Ryan and Cassidy into a predatory, fabricated tabloid narrative ("The Fatal Assumption") during the October 14, 1992 Friction sessions. Holly O'Connell intervened, won criminal and civil victories in 1994, reclaimed 100% of the band's masters, and founded Engine Room Records, LLC in-universe as an impenetrable artist sanctuary.

Dedicated Cosmic Portal (stardust.raggiesoft.com)

Because The Stardust Engine's biography, 12+ album eras, rolling sanctuary fleet (the 2002 Sainte-Claire 45H3 "The Iron Horse", the 2004 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 Launch Unit #001, and its 2015 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 replacement), and companion novels span four decades, their full band lore now resides on its own dedicated cosmic portal at stardust.raggiesoft.com.

Personnel & Roles

2. Band Members & Studio Collective

Ryan O'Connell

Co-Lead Vocals, Lead Electric Guitar & Lyricist

T10 paraplegic wheelchair user following the December 1990 I-81 black-ice crash; Cassidy's brother and safe person.

Cassidy O'Connell

Co-Lead Vocals, Analog Synthesizers, Piano & Chief Audio Architect

Pioneer of The Cosmic Tidal Lock Sound™ and composer of the 15-minute magnum opus "Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)."

Holly O'Connell, J.D., CFA

Manager, CEO (Engine Room Records, LLC) & Legal Architect

Architect of the 1992 Friction walkout, the 1994 Apex settlement, and the $2.4B O'Connell Family Revocable Trust; Class A CDL co-driver.

Evan Wright

Bass Guitar, Fretless Bass, Sub-Bass Synth Pedals & Systems

Identical twin maternal cousin; joined Ryan and Cassidy at CPI in 1986; Class A CDL co-driver.

Tyler Wright

Acoustic/Electronic Drums, Percussion & Fleet Logistics

Identical twin maternal cousin; joined Ryan and Cassidy at CPI in 1986; Class A CDL lead driver of The Iron Horse & RLFD30.

2004 Studio Album 11 Tracks

Progress Street

The 2004 Blacksburg Homecoming Album (Final Release Before the Burnout Hiatus)

A heartfelt, 1980s-inspired AOR and stadium synth-rock album from The Stardust Engine, recorded in 2004 at their home on Progress Street NE in Blacksburg, Virginia. Making the full-blooded 1980s melodic rock record that Apex Records never let them make in 1987, Progress Street celebrates collegiate roots, upright pianos, second-hand 1984 synthesizers, and unbreakable family unity—immortalized on the cover alongside the band's brand-new custom 2004 Prairie Coachworks RLFD30 low-floor shuttle coach before exhaustion forced them into their Burnout Hiatus.

2016 Live Album 34 Tracks

Live at the Crucible

3-Disc Live Box Set • Recorded Live Inside The Crucible (May 21, 2016) • Released Homecoming Weekend at the CPI Campus Bookstore (October 15, 2016)

The band's most important live album. Recorded live on Saturday, May 21, 2016 inside The Crucible in Blacksburg, Virginia—Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute's 65,000-seat stadium and the loudest house in all of college football—and released commercially during CPI Homecoming Weekend on October 15, 2016. With no opening act, CPI Alumni (Class of 1989) return home for a seven-act, 34-track career-spanning stadium show marking the final concert of a touring The Stardust Engine before launching their annual Forger Nation Summer Festival residency in Blacksburg in August 2017. Opens with the 300-piece CPI Marching Forgers ('Ignition: The Forger's Call', 'CPI Tech Triumph', and 'The Stardust Engine'), includes the ONLY recorded live performance of Cassidy's 13-minute magnum opus 'Escape Velocity (Ad Astra)' anchoring the 10-song Twin Moons cosmic journey (Act III: Cosmic Tidal Lock + Act IV: Roche Limit & Mile Marker 98), an intimate four-song acoustic block pairing Our Own Frequency with a stripped-down piano-and-acoustic-guitar rendition of 'Still Your Safe Person', the live concert debut of 'Saturday Night Lights: The Crucible', a hometown singalong on 'Neon on the Huckleberry Trail', a false ending on 'Last Bus Home: Lights Out on Progress Street', and the secret 5:26 1980s Stadium Rock (AOR) closing reclamation of 'Electric Color'.

2016 Compilation 16 Tracks

The Forger's Call

30th-Anniversary CPI & Blacksburg Archival Compilation (1986–2016) • Companion Anthology to Live at the Crucible

Released on CPI Homecoming Weekend (October 15, 2016) alongside Live at the Crucible—both as a companion anthology inside the Live at the Crucible 30th-Anniversary Box Set at the CPI Campus Bookstore and as a standalone archival compilation—The Forger's Call spans thirty years (1986–2016) of previously uncollected Commonwealth Polytechnic Institute (CPI) and Blacksburg vault recordings. Anchored at Track 1 by the official October 1986 Crucible Stadium Master of 'Ignition: The Forger's Call' (played over The Crucible PA system as the CPI Forgers football team charges onto the field) and closed at Track 16 by the original October 1986 Progress Street 4-track garage cassette ('Ignition: The Forger's Call [Demo Take 3]', where the band vocalizes 'TING... BOOM!' to test where the foundry anvil strikes), the 16-track compilation chronicles the band's entire Blacksburg collegiate and hometown history—from 1988 campus move-in anthem 'This Side of Heaven' and 1990 acoustic ballad 'Snowfall on Commonwealth Green' to 1992's 'One Dollar on the Kitchen Table', 1998's 'The Old Lady on the Hill' (Bennett Hall), and 2016's brass benediction 'Ad Astra, Per Aspera: Hymn for the Crucible'.
